1.why: All six screens are static, with no animations, carousels, or pop-ups — only a fixed header, a single card, and a static log panel.

2.why: Each screen has one large dark-blue heading and one filled primary blue button, so the main action stands out, though the dark 'Secure activity log' block visually competes for attention.

3.why: Each step presents a single field and a clear primary action, but the developer-style log panel and token strings add noise that a user must mentally filter out.

4.why: The flow is linear and one-step-at-a-time, but the user must still carry a long recovery token/6-digit code across screens and remember the 12-character password rules while typing.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, or show-password toggle appears on any screen, including the login/password creation step.

6.why: Nothing saved or familiar is surfaced — no saved email, masked account hint, or previously used device is shown; only the pre-filled recovery code in step 2 is recognizable.

7.why: Text is brief, plain-language, left-aligned, in a large readable font with short sentences and bullet lists on the privacy screen.

8.why: No error message is shown in any of the six screenshots, so there is no evidence the system describes problems and how to fix them.

9.why: Only a rules description exists ('at least 12 characters, ... a number, and a symbol') and helper text on the email field; no concrete example password or sample code format is provided.

10.why: Step 1 clearly offers 'Send recovery instructions' vs 'I have a recovery code', but no alternative login methods (face, passkey, biometric) exist to choose from.

11.why: Each screen offers at most two buttons and one or two input fields, so choice load is minimal.

12.why: Steps 5 and 6 confirm the outcome explicitly ('Your account access has been confirmed', 'Your acceptance has been securely recorded'), though no confirmation is shown after saving the new password or verifying the code.

13.why: Short guidance/tip boxes appear on several steps (safety notice, password rules, code delivery explanation), but there is no help link, progress indicator, or contextual tips for the MFA and privacy steps.

14.why: Only step 2 offers a 'Back' button; other steps have no retry, resend-code, cancel, or edit option, so recovering from a mistake is unclear.

15.why: Every screen reuses the same header, card layout, heading style, blue primary button, info-box styling, and footer notice.
